name: BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Ltd
title: BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Ltd - 544484 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue up 49% to INR 733 cr with pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin 7.5% (+273 bps); supply-side discipline is not evidenced, and management is guiding ~20% store CAGR with no capex or capacity figures.

triggers.label: Inventory ~INR 2,800 cr vs 2,650 cr in March
Same-store sales growth 39%
triggers.quote: our same-store sales growth of 39%, which was broad-based

triggers.label: Revenue ~INR 12,000 cr in four years; 50% CAGR math disputed
triggers.quote: distribution growth taking the overall revenue to around INR 12,000 number in the next four years

summary.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 49% YoY to INR 733 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 135% to INR 55 crore, lifting operating margin to 7.5% (up 273 bps). Management attributed this to operating leverage despite a custom duty hike on gold from 6% to 15% that softened demand in May before June and July recovered. Same-store sales growth was 39%, repeat revenue share rose to about 60%, while new customer additions reportedly fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management tied to merchandise dislocation during the sharp gold rise. Management reiterated a long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years, around 30% SSSG and about 20% store distribution growth, though analysts questioned the arithmetic.

financial_highlights.value: About INR 50 crore, about 6.9% of revenue
financial_highlights.change: Flat vs 6.9% in same quarter last year
Up from INR 2,650 crore at March

segments.name: Online / omnichannel
segments.commentary: Management said more than 80% of sales originate online, with stores converting intent built online. Company describes itself as a consumer internet business that sells jewellery.

segments.name: Stores
segments.commentary: Network of 352 stores; recent stores are around 4,500 sq ft frontage, and management said operational sq ft and per-store unit economics are unchanged. Store additions guided to about 20% CAGR over four years, with a 70-80 annual run rate referenced.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: About 95% of products sold are manufactured in-house; management estimates a 300-400 bps margin delta versus peers but stresses design control as the main rationale.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years (from INR 2,440 crore in FY26), with around 30% SSSG on mature cohorts plus about 20% distribution growth.
Operating EBITDA margin expected to expand from 7.5% toward about 15% over four years, driven mainly by corporate and marketing scale leverage.
Marketing spend guided to fall from 6.6% of revenue in FY26 to about 4.5-4.6% over five years, with FY27 expected below 6.6%.
Blended inventory turn expected to improve towards 1.7-1.8x over four years, with improvement visible in FY27.
Store additions described as non-linear, but the 20% distribution growth trend line is expected to be retained through FY27.
capex_capacity: Store area grew about 25.5% YoY while rent expense grew about 35%; annual lease escalation is 3-5%.
Newer stores are larger (around 4,500 sq ft frontage) to add capacity, with management saying per-store rent and revenue are not materially different.
Older cohorts are said to deliver store-level ROIC around 40% at 1.8-2.0x inventory turns.
Around 20% distribution (store) CAGR guided over next four years; store additions expected to be non-linear.
demand_pricing: Demand softened in May after the gold import duty hike (6% to 15%), then recovered through June; management said July trends were similar to June.
Gold exchange volumes rose as gold prices climbed; management said no significant change in the last 1-2 weeks.
New customer additions fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management attributed to merchandise dislocation; repeat revenue growth was strong.
Repeat AOVs are said to be 20-30% higher than new-customer AOVs; blended AOV about INR 78,000.
Management says no 9-carat plans; 14-carat experiments are used in lower price points. Lab-grown diamonds are said to be under 1% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand trending into July after the May softness from the duty hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand softened in May, recovered through June, and July is tracking similarly to June with no major difference.

qa_highlights.question: How should growth be thought of in H2 as gold inflation tapers, and the company lapping sharp gold rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stable gold is most supportive for demand and that Q3 last year was its slowest quarter in history during the sharpest gold rise; it does not expect a headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Why has new customer addition fallen to about 40,000 and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the drop, attributed it to merchandise dislocation being fixed, and said month-on-month new customer trends are improving.

qa_highlights.question: Math behind the 50% revenue CAGR given 30% SSSG and 20% distribution growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% refers to mature-cohort SSSG at maturity (years 3-6), not reported SSSG, and that reported SSSG would be higher due to new stores.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin expanded about 100 bps excluding inventory gain; what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix changes in studded share were not material; contribution margin, the more relevant metric, has been largely stable, and EBITDA expansion comes from operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory: what is the figure and why did it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about INR 2,800 crore at end June versus INR 2,650 crore in March; management said store additions and gold prices drive the balance and turns should improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why 20% distribution growth rather than a slower pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most operating leverage comes from corporate and marketing scale rather than store-level profit, so faster distribution growth is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: Marketing spend trend and percent of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was about INR 50 crore, 6.9% of revenue, same as last year; it fell from about 9.2% four years ago to 6.6% in FY26.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility and import duty changes (6% to 15%) affecting demand, merchandise mix and inventory levels.
Slowing new customer additions (about 40,000 vs about 50,000 earlier) and whether merchandise dislocation is resolved.
Gap between reported SSSG and the 30% long-term SSSG used to underpin the 50% revenue CAGR target.
Rent growth (35%) outpacing store area growth (25.5%), and whether store productivity keeps pace with expansion.
Inventory turn trajectory from current level toward 1.7-1.8x, and inventory balance at the next quarter-end.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and long-term targets, but evasive on reported SSSG arithmetic, new customer targets and inventory data (declined to give kg or detailed AOV). Management stressed that quarterly numbers are noisy and that analysts should focus on cohort and per-store metrics.
key_quotes: Q1 marks a strong start to the year.
That relationship, revenue scaling against a cost base that rose far more slowly, is the operating leverage in our model becoming visible.
So if gold stays range-bound, it's even better for us.
We are the only jewellery company that has built its entire technology stack in-house.

adds.what: Store network expansion: about 20% store distribution CAGR over four years, with 70-80 stores added per year run rate referenced (network of 352 stores today);

growth.why: Management reiterated ~INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years (about 50% CAGR from INR 2,440 crore FY26) backed by ~20% store distribution CAGR (352 stores, 70-80 added per year) and ~30% SSSG; Q1 revenue +49% and SSSG +39% support near-term momentum, but analysts questioned the arithmetic and no order book or specific capacity schedule was given beyond the store run rate.
